name: Alsace grand cru Schoenenbourg

land: Faces toward the sun, which warms the vines and helps the grapes ripen.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
One of 51 named grand cru vineyards, each its own appellation. The wine must come from that vineyard, name it on the label and meet stricter rules than plain Alsace AOC.
Late harvest. The grapes need at least 244 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 270 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.
Made from grapes with noble rot. They need at least 276 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 306 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.

blurb.text: An Alsace Grand Cru vineyard in Riquewihr and Zellenberg. Its wines can be made from six grapes: Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and three Muscats (Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains, Muscat Rose à Petits Grains and Muscat Ottonel). Each white is made from one grape alone, though the Muscats may be blended.
